Steve Long, Operations Director for Public Works, explained that this grant would pay for the bulkhead replacement along the Northbank from the CSX building down to Metropolitan Park.

CM Lahnen stated that $126 million had already been budgeted on the Northbank Bulkhead project and asked Mr. Long whether the Public Works Department could provide an update to the Council regarding progress, and Mr. Long responded that he would be able to do so.

Regarding bill 2024-0033, CM Gay asked whether the Public Works department could transfer funds from the Northbank Bulkhead project to the Southbank Bulkhead project without violating the grant agreement. Phillip Peterson of the Council Auditor's Office clarified that grant funds would not be transferred; the grant funding freed up funds that could be transferred from the Northbank Bulkhead Project to the Southbank Bulkhead project.

CM Boylan asked whether this was the first FDEP grant received for the Northbank Bulkhead Project, and Mr. Long responded that it was.

CM Carlucci asked whether the Public Works Department could provide an update on the progress of Riverfront parks projects.

m-jacksonville|2024-02-20|f0cd8e34|c5790.title:
Phillip Peterson explained the amendment. CM Carlucci talked about the tremendous need for this program because many homeowners are in dire straits with regard to potentially losing their homeowners insurance coverage because their insurance companies require a new roof to continue coverage. Travis Jeffrey of the Housing and Community Development Division described how the initial program launched in January and was oversubscribed in the first half hour of availability. 16 of the first 20 selected applications were approved, the projects are being bundled and bid out through the Procurement Division, and construction will begin in the next few weeks. Council President Salem asked about what happens if the owner of a home on which a roof is installed sells the property. Mr. Jeffrey said if the owner sells the property in less than 5 years, there is a lien that must be repaid. Their staff checks ownership status every year. In response to a question from CM Lahnen, he explained how the applications were evaluated and what happens when the cost of the roof exceeds what the owner can afford above the City’s contribution. 

CM Diamond said he opposes the program on the grounds that it is not something the City should be doing and is a transfer of wealth from some council districts to others and from some taxpayers to others against their will. CM Freeman asked about how roofing contractors are selected and monitored. Mr. Jeffries said all payment is done on a reimbursement basis

It is done in ordinance form because it includes an Ordinance Code waiver and provides mostly 1-year projects in addition to a long-term strategy of allocating $5M per year to a strategic downtown major projects fund. The short-term projects are grouped into strategic categories. Council Member Diamond’s proposed project for a $200,000 allocation to Atlantic Beach to assist with construction of a lifeguard station was added after the last meeting after Mr. Diamond returned from his military deployment. The committee authorized introduction of the legislation as a Finance Committee bill on next week’s Council agenda.
